Among them: the site of his mosque (ﷺ) was a graveyard of the polytheists. He had their graves dug up and levelled, and took the place as a mosque, and did not remove the soil, but leveled the ground, smoothed it, and prayed in it, as established in the Two Sahihs from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

"When the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Medina and alighted at the upper part of Medina, in a quarter called Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, the Prophet (ﷺ) stayed among them for fourteen nights. Then he sent for the chiefs of Banu al-Najjar, and they came with their swords hung, and it is as if I see the Prophet (ﷺ) upon his mount, with Abu Bakr behind him, and the chiefs of Banu al-Najjar around him, until he alighted in the courtyard of Abu Ayyub.

He loved to pray wherever prayer overtook him, and he prayed in the sheepfolds. He commanded the building of the mosque, and sent for the chiefs of Banu al-Najjar and said: 'O Banu al-Najjar, name a price for this garden of yours.'

They said: 'No, by Allah, we seek its price only from Allah.' In it, as I tell you, were graves of the polytheists, and in it were ruins and palm trees. The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded that the graves of the polytheists be dug up, then the ruins were levelled, and the palm trees were cut down. They arranged the palm trees facing the qibla of the mosque, and made its two side posts of stone. They began carrying the rock, and they were chanting rajaz."

And he mentioned the hadith...

Among them: the fitna of shirk through praying at graves and imitating idol-worshippers is far greater than the harm of praying after ʿAsr and Fajr. So if this is forbidden as a blocking of the pretext of imitation, which hardly occurs to the one praying, how much more so this near pretext which often leads its doer to shirk and calling upon the dead, seeking their help, asking them for needs, and believing that prayer at their graves is better than in the mosques, and other things which are open opposition to Allah and His Messenger.

Where then is the reasoning of impurity of the place in relation to this corruption?

And among what shows that the Prophet (ﷺ) intended to protect this community from the trial with graves, as the people of Noah and those after them were tried by them:

Among them: he cursed those who take mosques upon them. Had it been because of impurity, it would have been possible to build a mosque upon them while plastering them with pure clay, and the curse would cease, and this is certainly false.

Among them: he linked in the curse those who take mosques over them with those who light lamps upon them. They are companions in the curse.

And they are equal in committing a major sin. For everything the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed is a major sin, and it is known that lighting lamps upon them was cursed only because it is a means to venerating them and making them a shrine to which the polytheists resort, as is the reality. Likewise taking mosques over them.

That is why he linked them. For taking mosques over them is veneration of them and an exposure to the trial through them. Thus Allah, glory be to Him, related of those who prevailed over the affair of the People of the Cave that they said: ﴿We will surely take over them a place of worship﴾ [al-Kahf: 21].

Among them: the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"O Allah, do not make my grave an idol that is worshipped. The anger of Allah has intensified against a people who took the graves of their prophets as mosques."

He mentioned this right after his words: "O Allah, do not make my grave an idol that is worshipped," as an indication of the cause for the curse falling upon them, namely their means to make them idols worshipped.

In sum, whoever has knowledge of shirk, its causes and its pretexts, and understood from the Messenger (ﷺ) his intentions, will be certain beyond any doubt that this emphasis of his in cursing and forbidding, with both its forms, "do not do" and "I forbid you," is not because of impurity, but because of the impurity of shirk that attaches to whoever disobeys him, commits what he forbade, follows his desire, does not fear his Lord and Master, and whose share is small or nonexistent in realizing the testimony that there is no god but Allah. For this and similar things from the Prophet (ﷺ) are a protection of the sanctuary of monotheism from being touched and covered by shirk, and a dedication to it and anger for his Lord lest anything be equated with Him.

But the polytheists refused except to disobey his command and commit what he forbade, and Satan deceived them.

He said: "Rather, this is veneration of the graves of shaykhs and the righteous."

"The more you venerate them, and the more extreme you are about them, the closer you will be to them in happiness, and the farther from their enemies."

By the life of Allah, it was through this very door that entry was made upon the worshippers of Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr, and through it entry was made upon the worshippers of idols from their time until the Day of Resurrection. The polytheists combined extremism regarding them with defaming their path, while Allah guided the people of monotheism to follow their path, and to place them in the station Allah placed them: servitude, and the stripping away from them of the distinctive attributes of divinity. This is the utmost of veneration and obedience to them.

As for the polytheists, they disobeyed their command, and belittled them in the form of veneration.

Al-Shafiʿi said: "I dislike that a created being be venerated to the extent that his grave is made a mosque, out of fear of the trial upon him and upon those after him among the people."

Among those who gave the reason as shirk and imitation of the Jews and Christians: al-Athram, in his book "Nasikh al-Hadith wa Mansukhuhu." He said, after mentioning the hadith of Abu Saʿid that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The earth has been made a mosque for me, except the graveyard and the bathhouse," and the hadith of Zayd ibn Jubayr from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from Nafi' from Ibn ʿUmar that the Prophet (ﷺ) "forbade prayer in seven places, and mentioned among them the graveyard":

Al-Athram said: "I only disliked prayer in the graveyard because of imitation of the People of the Book, for they take the graves of their prophets and righteous ones as mosques."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 71, verse 21–24 (part 1 of 2):

Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both):
"These are the names of righteous men from the people of Nuh. When they died, Satan inspired their people: 'Set up stone idols (ansab) at the gathering places where they used to sit, and name them after them.' They did so, but they were not worshipped until those (people) died and knowledge was forgotten, and then they were worshipped."

Ibn Jarir said, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: "They were righteous men among the children of Adam. They had followers who emulated them. When they died, their companions, who used to emulate them, said: 'If we made their images, it would be more stirring for us to worship when we remember them.' So they made their images. When they died and others came after them, Iblis crept up to them and said: 'They used only to worship them, and by them rain was sought, so they worshipped them.'"

Hisham ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kalbi said: My father informed me, who said:
"The first idol-worship occurred when Adam (peace be upon him) died. The sons of Shith ibn Adam placed him in a cave on the mountain upon which Adam had been sent down, in the land of India. The mountain is called Nudh, and it is the most fertile mountain on earth."

Hisham said: My father informed me, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The sons of Shith (peace be upon him) would come to the body of Adam in the cave, glorify it, and pray for mercy upon him. A man from the sons of Qabil ibn Adam said: 'O sons of Qabil, the sons of Shith have a rite they perform around it, glorifying it, and you have nothing.' So he carved an idol for them, and he was the first to make it."

Hisham said: My father also informed me: "Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr were righteous people who died in one month. Their close relatives grieved for them. A man from the sons of Qabil said: 'O people, would you like me to carve for you five idols in their likenesses? However, I cannot put spirits into them.' They said: 'Yes.' So he carved for them five idols in their likenesses and set them up for them. A man would go to his brother, his uncle, and his cousin, glorify it, and circle around it, until that first generation passed away. These had been made in the time of Barad ibn Mahla'il ibn Qaynan ibn Anush ibn Shith ibn Adam. Then another generation came and glorified them more intensely than the first generation. Then came a third generation after them, and they said: 'Our forefathers only glorified these because they hoped for their intercession with Allah, the Exalted.' So they worshipped them, magnified their matter, and their disbelief grew severe. Allah sent to them Idris (peace be upon him) as a prophet, and he called them, but they denied him. So Allah raised him to a lofty place. Their matter continued to intensify," as Ibn al-Kalbi related from Abu al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, "until Nuh (peace be upon him) came, and Allah sent him as a prophet. He was then four hundred and eighty years old. He called them to Allah in his prophethood for one hundred and twenty years, but they disobeyed and denied him. Allah commanded him to build the Ark. He finished it and boarded it when he was six hundred years old. Those who were to drown drowned, and he remained after that three hundred and fifty years, calling them to Allah."

And there were two thousand two hundred years between Adam and Nuh. The water carried these idols from land to land until it cast them onto the land of Jeddah. When the water receded and they were left on the shore, the wind blew sand over them until it covered them."

I say: The apparent meaning of the Qur'an contradicts this, and that Nuh (peace be upon him) remained among his people for a thousand years less fifty years, and that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, destroyed them by drowning after they had lived among them for this period.

Al-Kalbi said: 'Amr ibn Luhayy was a soothsayer who had a familiar spirit from the jinn: "Hasten the departure and the journey from Tihama, with fortune and safety." He said: "Jir (go), and do not stay." He said: "Go to the sandbank of Jeddah, and you will find there idols prepared. Bring them to Tihama and do not be unsettled, then call the Arabs to worship them, and they will respond." So he went to the river of Jeddah, extracted them, then carried them until he arrived at Tihama. The pilgrimage season came, and he called the Arabs to worship them, all of them. 'Awf ibn 'Adhra ibn Zayd al-Lat, son of Rufayda ibn Thawr ibn Kalb ibn Wabara ibn Taghlib ibn Hulwan ibn Imran ibn al-Haf ibn Qudha'a, responded to him, and he gave him Wadd. He carried it and it was at Wadi al-Qura, at Dumat al-Jandal. He named his son 'Abd-Wadd, and he was the first to be named with it. He appointed 'Arf, his son 'Amir, who is called 'Amir al-Ajdar, as its custodian. His descendants continued to serve it until Allah brought Islam."

Al-Kalbi said: "Malik ibn Harithah told me that he saw Wadd. He said: 'My father used to send me with milk to it, and he would say: "Give your god to drink," and I would drink it.' He said: 'Then I saw Khalid ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) after he broke it, and he made it into fragments.'"

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to demolish it, but the Banu 'Adhra and the Banu 'Amir al-Ajdar prevented him from demolishing it. He fought them, killed them, demolished it and broke it.

Al-Kalbi said: "I said to Malik ibn Harithah: 'Describe Wadd to me, as if I were looking at it.' He said: 'It was the statue of a man, as large as the greatest of men, decorated (dubbira, i.e., carved) with two garments: wrapped in one garment and covered with another. On it was a sword that he wore on his shoulder, and he had slung a bow, and before him was a spear with a banner, and a quiver containing arrows,' meaning a case."

He said: "The narration returned."

He said: "Amr ibn Luhayy also answered Mudar ibn Nizar. He gave to a man from Hudhayl called al-Harith ibn Tamim ibn Sa'd ibn Hudhayl ibn Mudrikah ibn Ilyas ibn Mudar: Suwa'. It was in a land called Wahat, in the valley of Nakhla, and those near to it from Mudar worshipped it."

Regarding this, a man of the Arabs said:
"You see them around their qibla, devoted, as Hudhayl devoted themselves to Suwa'.
Its surroundings lie slain before it, the treasures of every shepherd."

Mudhhij answered him, so he gave to An'um ibn 'Amr al-Muradi Yaghuth. It was on a hill in Yemen, worshipped by Mudhhij and those allied to them.

Hamdan answered him, so he gave to Malik ibn Murthid ibn Jushum ibn Hashid ibn Jushum ibn Khayran ibn Nawf ibn Hamdan: Ya'uq. It was in a village called Khayawan, worshipped by Hamdan and those allied to them from Yemen.

Himyar answered: he gave to a man from Dhu Ru'ayn called Ma'd Yakrib: Nasr. It was in a place in the land of Saba called Balkha', worshipped by Himyar and those allied to them. They continued to worship it until Dhu Nawas made them Jews.

These idols continued to be worshipped until Allah sent the Prophet (ﷺ), who demolished and broke them.

I say: This is an explanation of what al-Bukhari mentioned in his Sahih from Ibn 'Abbas, who said:
"The idols that were among the people of Nuh passed into the Arabs. As for Wadd, it belonged to Kalb at Dumat al-Jandal. As for Suwa', it belonged to Hudhayl. As for Yaghuth, it belonged to Murad, then to the Banu Ghutayf, at al-Huruf near Saba. As for Ya'uq, it belonged to Hamdan. As for Nasr, it belonged to Himyar, to the family of Dhu al-Kala'. He said: 'These are the names of righteous men from the people of Nuh.'"

And he mentioned what preceded.

In the Sahih of al-Bukhari, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"I saw 'Amr ibn 'Amir al-Khuza'i dragging his intestines in the Fire, and he was the first to release the sawa'ib (free-roaming beasts)."

In another wording: "and he altered the religion of Ibrahim."

Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith al-Taymi related to me that Abu Salih al-Samman told him that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to Aktham ibn al-Jawn al-Khuza'i:
"O Aktham, I saw 'Amr ibn Luhayy ibn Qam'ah ibn Khindif dragging his intestines in the Fire. I have never seen a man more similar to a man than he is to you, nor you to him." Aktham said: "May his likeness harm me, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "No, you are a believer and he is a disbeliever. He was the first to alter the religion of Isma'il: he set up idols, slit the ears of the she-camel (bahira), released the free-roaming beast (sa'iba), made the she-camel that bears ten young ones a wasila, and protected the stallion (ham)."

Ibn Hisham said: Some of the people of knowledge related to me: "'Amr ibn Luhayy went out from Mecca to Syria on some of his affairs. When he arrived at Ma'ab in the land of al-Balqa', where the 'Amaliqah were at that time, sons of 'Amlaq ibn Lawidh ibn Sam ibn Nuh, he saw them worshipping idols. He said to them: 'What are these idols that you worship?' They said: 'We seek rain by them, and they give us rain; we seek victory by them, and they give us victory.' He said: 'Will you not give me one of them, so that I may take it to the land of the Arabs and they may worship it?' So they gave him an idol called Hubal. He came with it to Mecca, set it up, and commanded the people to worship and glorify it."

Hisham said: My father and others related to me: "When Isma'il (peace be upon him) settled in Mecca and his children were born there, they multiplied until they filled Mecca, and they expelled those of the 'Amaliqah who were there. Mecca became too narrow for them, wars and enmities arose among them, and some of them expelled others. So they spread out across the lands seeking livelihood. What led them to worship idols and stones was that no traveler would depart from Mecca without carrying with him a stone from the stones of the Haram, out of reverence for the Haram and longing for Mecca. Wherever they settled they would place it and circle it as they circled the House, out of love for the House and longing for it. They still glorified the House and Mecca, performed the hajj and 'umrah, upon the inheritance of Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them both). Then they worshipped what they found good and forgot what they had been upon, and they exchanged the religion of Ibrahim for another, worshipping idols, and they came to be like the nations before them. They brought out from the idols what the people of Nuh had worshipped, following what remained of their memory among them. Among them there remained, from the time of Ibrahim and Isma'il, remnants of worship, by which they practised devotion: glorifying the House, circling it, the hajj and 'umrah, standing at 'Arafat and Muzdalifah, and offering the sacrificial camels, while introducing into it what was not part of it." Nizar used to say in their talbiyah:
"Here I am, O Allah, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner."
"Except a partner who is Yours, You possess him and he does not possess."

They affirmed His oneness by the talbiyah, yet they brought their gods alongside Him and made their ownership in His hand. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to His Prophet (ﷺ):
﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah without associating others with Him.﴾ [Yusuf: 106]
That is, they do not affirm My oneness with true knowledge of My right, except that they set up a partner alongside Me from among My creation.

The talbiyah of 'Akk, when they set out as pilgrims, was that they sent two black boys ahead of them. They would walk in front of their caravan and say:
"We are the two crows of 'Akk."
Then 'Akk would say after them:
"'Akk, to You is your servant, the Yemenite servants of Yours."

When Rabi'ah performed the hajj and completed the rites and stood at the standing-places, they would depart in the first group and not remain until the last days of Tashriq.

The first to alter the religion of Isma'il, setting up idols, releasing the free-roaming beast (sa'iba), slitting the ears of the she-camel (bahira), making the wasila, and protecting the stallion (ham), was 'Amr ibn Rabi'ah, who is Luhayy ibn Harithah ibn 'Amr ibn 'Amir al-Azdi, and he is the father of Khuza'ah.

The mother of 'Amr was Fuhayrah bint 'Amir ibn al-Harith; it is also said Qam'ah bint Mudad. The Harith who was in charge of the affairs of the Ka'bah, when 'Amr ibn Luhayy came of age, disputed the leadership with him, and he fought Jurhum with the sons of Isma'il. He defeated them, drove them out from the Ka'bah, and expelled them from the lands of Mecca.

He took over the guardianship of the House after them. Then he fell severely ill, and it was said to him: "In al-Balqa' of Syria there is hot springs; if you go there you will be healed." He went there, bathed in it, and was healed. He found its people worshipping idols and said: "What are these?" They said: "We seek rain by them and seek victory over the enemy by them." He asked them to give him some of them, and they did, so he brought them to Mecca and set them up around the Ka'bah.

The Arabs adopted idols. The earliest of them was Manat, and the Arabs used to name themselves 'Abd Manat and Zayd Manat. It was set up on the seacoast in the direction of al-Mushallal near Qudayd, between Mecca and Medina, and all the Arabs glorified it. The Aws and Khazraj and those who lived in Medina and Mecca and the nearby places glorified it, slaughtering for it and offering gifts to it. The sons of Ma'd were upon a remnant of the religion of Isma'il. Rabi'ah and Mudar were upon a remnant of his religion, and none were more intense in glorifying it than the Aws and Khazraj.

Hisham said: A man of Quraysh related to us from Abu 'Ubaydah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi 'Ubaydah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ammar ibn Yasir, who said:
"The Aws and Khazraj and those who neighboured them from the Arabs of Yathrib and elsewhere used to perform the hajj, standing with the people at all the standing-places. They did not shave their heads. When they dispersed, they would come to it and shave their heads there, and they remained there, not regarding their hajj as complete except by that."

Manat belonged to Hudhayl and Khuza'ah. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) sent 'Ali, who demolished it in the year of the Conquest.

Then they took al-Lat at al-Ta'if, which was more recent than Manat. It was a square rock, and a Jew used to grind sawiq (parched grain) at it. Its custodians were the Banu 'Attab ibn Malik of Thaqif, and they had built a structure over it. Quraysh and all the Arabs glorified it, and by it the Arabs used to name themselves Zayd al-Lat and Taym al-Lat. It was at the place where the left minaret of the mosque of al-Ta'if stands today.

It remained so until Thaqif embraced Islam. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who demolished it and burned it with fire.

Then they took al-Uzza, which was more recent than al-Lat and Manat. Zalim ibn As'ad took it. It was in a valley of Nakhlah al-Shamiyah called Hurad, opposite al-Ghumayr, on the right side of the one ascending to Iraq from Mecca. That is beyond Dhat 'Irq, and they built a house over it. They used to hear a sound from it.

Hisham said: My father related to me from Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-'Uzza was a female devil who came to three acacia trees in the valley of Nakhlah. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Mecca, he sent Khalid ibn al-Walid, saying: 'Go to the valley of Nakhlah, for you will find three acacias; cut down the first.' He went and cut it down. When he came back to him, he said: 'Did you see anything?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Cut down the second.' He went and cut it down. Then he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'Did you see anything?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Cut down the third.' He went and found an Abyssinian woman with disheveled hair, placing her hands on her shoulders, gnashing with her fangs, and behind her was Dubayyah ibn Hurmi al-Shaybani, then al-Sulami, who was her custodian. When she saw Khalid, she said:
'O 'Uzza, strike with strength, do not be false, against Khalid, cast off your veil and gird up your skirts.
For if you do not kill Khalid today, you will be humiliated quickly and be made Christian.'
Khalid said:
'O 'Uzza, disbelief in you, no glorification of you, for I have seen that Allah has humiliated you.'
Then he struck her and split her head, and she was a black lump of charcoal. Then he cut down the tree, and killed the custodian, and then came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him. He said: 'That was al-'Uzza, and there will be no 'Uzza for the Arabs after her. Indeed, she will not be worshipped after today.'"

(Section)

Among the greatest of his schemes, by which he deceived most people, and from which none escaped except those whom Allah did not intend to test, is what he inspired, from of old and in recent times, into his party and allies: the temptation through graves. Until the matter ended with them worshipping their masters besides Allah, and their graves were worshipped, and they took them as idols, built temples over them, carved the images of their masters in them, then those images became bodies with shadows, then they were made idols and worshipped alongside Allah, the Exalted.

The beginning of this great disease was among the people of Nuh, as He, glorified is He, told of them in His Book, where He says:
﴿Nuh said: "My Lord, they disobeyed me and followed one whom his wealth and children increased only in loss. And they schemed a great scheme. And they said: 'Do not leave your gods; do not leave Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr.' And they have led many astray..."﴾ [Nuh: 21–24]

Ibn Jarir said:
"What was reported to us about these was what Ibn Humayd related to us: Mahran related to us from Sufyan from Musa from Muhammad ibn Qays, that Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr were righteous men among the children of Adam. They had followers who emulated them. When they died, their companions who used to emulate them said: 'If we made their images, it would be more stirring for us to worship when we remember them.' So they made their images. When they died and others came after them, Iblis crept up to them and said: 'They only worshipped them, and by them rain was sought, so they worshipped them.'"

Sufyan related from his father from 'Ikrimah, who said: "Between Adam and Nuh (peace be upon them both) there were ten generations, all upon Islam."

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us from Ma'mar from Qatadah regarding this verse, who said: "They were gods worshipped by the people of Nuh, and then the Arabs worshipped them after that. Wadd was for Kalb at Dumat al-Jandal, and Suwa' was for Hudhayl. Yaghuth was for the Banu Ghutayf of Murad. Ya'uq was for Hamdan. Nasr was for Dhu al-Kala' of Himyar."

Al-Walibi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "These are idols that were worshipped in the time of Nuh (peace be upon him)."

Al-Bukhari said: Ibrahim ibn Musa related to us: Hisham related to us from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' said from Ibn 'Abbas:
"The idols that were among the people of Nuh passed into the Arabs after that.
As for Wadd, it belonged to Kalb at Dumat al-Jandal.
As for Suwa', it belonged to Hudhayl."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 71, verse 21–24 (part 2 of 2):

As for Yaghuth, it belonged to Murad, then to the Banu Ghutayf at al-Jurf near Saba'.
As for Ya'uq, it belonged to Hamdan.
As for Nasr, it belonged to Himyar, to the family of Dhu al-Kala'.

They were the names of righteous men from the people of Noah. When they died, Satan inspired their people to set up idols (anṣāb) at the gatherplaces where they used to sit, and to name them after them. They did so, but they were not worshipped until those men had died and knowledge had been forgotten, and then they were worshipped."

Another scholar among the early generations (al-salaf) said: These were righteous men among the people of Noah, peace be upon him. When they died, the people remained devoted at their graves, then they made images of them, then time lengthened over them and they worshipped them.

These people combined two trials: the trial of graves and the trial of images. These are the two trials to which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pointed in the hadith agreed upon as authentic, narrated from ʿĀʾisha (may Allah be pleased with her):

"Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her) mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a church she had seen in the land of Abyssinia, called Maria. She described to him the images she had seen in it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Those are a people who, when a righteous servant or a righteous man among them died, built a place of worship (masjid) over his grave and made those images in it. Those are the worst of creation in the sight of Allah, the Exalted.'"

In another wording in the Two Sahihs:

"Umm Habibah and Umm Salamah mentioned a church they had seen."

So in this hadith he combined images and graves, and this was the cause of the worship of al-Lat.

Ibn Jarir narrated with his chain from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding:

﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-ʿUzza?﴾ [al-Najm: 19]

He said: "He used to knead the sawiq (a porridge of roasted grain) for them. When he died, they remained devoted at his grave." Similarly Abu al-Jawza said, from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both):

"He used to knead the sawiq for the pilgrims."

Thus you have seen that the cause of the worship of Wadd, Yaghuth, Ya'uq, Nasr and al-Lat was only the veneration of their graves, and then they made images of them and worshipped them, as the Prophet (ﷺ) indicated.

My shaykh said: "This is the reason for which the Lawgiver forbade taking mosques upon graves, and it is what led many nations either into major shirk or into what is less than it. Souls have associated partners with Allah through the images of righteous people, and through images they claim are talismans for the stars and the like. Shirk directed at the grave of a man believed to be righteous is closer to souls than shirk directed at a piece of wood or a stone. This is why we find the people of shirk often humbling themselves there, becoming submissive and lowly, and worshipping them in their hearts with a worship they do not perform in the houses of Allah or at the time of dawn. Some of them prostrate to them. Most of them hope for blessing from prayer and supplication there what they do not hope for in the mosques.

Because of this corruption, the Prophet (ﷺ) cut off its source, to the extent that he forbade prayer in the graveyard absolutely, even if the one praying does not intend the blessing of the place by his prayer, as he intends the blessing of the mosques. Likewise he forbade prayer at the time of sunrise and sunset, because these are times when the polytheists intend to pray to the sun. So he forbade his community to pray at those times, even if the one praying does not intend what the polytheists intended, as a blocking of the means (sadd al-dhara'i')."

He said: As for when a man intends to pray at graves seeking blessing by praying in that spot, this is precisely deceiving Allah and His Messenger, opposing His religion, and innovating a religion Allah did not permit. The Muslims have agreed, on what they know necessarily from the religion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that praying at graves is forbidden, and that he cursed whoever takes them as mosques. So among the greatest innovations and causes of shirk is praying at them and taking them as mosques, and building mosques upon them. The texts from the Prophet, peace be upon him, forbidding this and warning strongly against it have been transmitted by multiple chains. Most schools have explicitly stated the prohibition of building mosques over them, following the sound and clear Sunnah. The companions of Ahmad and others from the companions of Malik and al-Shafiʿi have explicitly stated its prohibition. A group stated it as merely disliked (makruh) without qualification. What should be understood is that it refers to the disliked in the sense of prohibition (karahat al-tahrim), out of good opinion of the scholars, and one should not think of them that they would permit what has been transmitted by multiple chains from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as cursing its doer and forbidding it. In Sahih Muslim, from Jundub ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Bajali, who said:

I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) five days before he died saying:

"I disown before Allah that I should have a close friend (khalil) among you. Indeed Allah has taken me as a close friend, as He took Ibrahim as a close friend. Had I taken a close friend from my community, I would have taken Abu Bakr as a close friend. Beware, those before you used to take the graves of their prophets as mosques. Beware, do not take graves as mosques, for I forbid you from that."

And from ʿĀʾisha and ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas, who both said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was near death, he began placing a cloak over his face, and when he felt distress he uncovered it, and he said, while in that state: 'The curse of Allah be upon the Jews and the Christians, who took the graves of their prophets as mosques,' warning against what they did."

Agreed upon.

Also in the Two Sahihs, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him):

That the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah fight the Jews and the Christians, who took the graves of their prophets as mosques."

In Muslim's narration: "May Allah curse the Jews and the Christians, who took the graves of their prophets as mosques."

So he forbade taking graves as mosques at the end of his life, and then he cursed, while in his last moments, those from the People of the Book who did that, in order to warn his community against doing the same.

ʿĀʾisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said during his illness from which he did not rise: "May Allah curse the Jews and the Christians, who took the graves of their prophets as mosques. Had it not been for that, his grave would have been made conspicuous, but it was feared that it would be taken as a mosque."

Agreed upon.

Her words "khushiya" (it was feared) are with a damma on the kha', as the reason for not exposing his grave.

Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad, with a good chain, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Among the most evil of people are those on whom the Hour will come while they are alive, and those who take graves as mosques."

From Zayd ibn Thabit, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah curse the Jews, who took the graves of their prophets as mosques." Narrated by Imam Ahmad.

From Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the women who visit graves, and those who take mosques and lamps upon them." Narrated by Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan.

In Sahih al-Bukhari: that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) saw Anas ibn Malik praying at a grave, and said: "The grave! The grave!" This shows that it was well established among the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) that their Prophet had forbidden them to pray at graves. Anas's action (may Allah be pleased with him) does not indicate his belief in its permissibility, for perhaps he had not seen it, or did not know it was a grave, or he was heedless of it. When ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) alerted him, he became mindful.

Abu Saʿid al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The whole earth is a mosque except the graveyard and the bathhouse."

Narrated by Imam Ahmad and the authors of the four Sunan, and authenticated by Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban.

More emphatic than this: he forbade praying facing a grave, so that a grave is not between the one praying and the qibla.

Muslim narrated in his Sahih, from Abu Marthad al-Ghanawi (may Allah have mercy on him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not sit upon graves, and do not pray facing them."

In this is a refutation of the view of those who claim that the prohibition of praying there is due to impurity (najasa). This is the furthest thing from the intentions of the Messenger (ﷺ), and it is false for several reasons:

Among them: the hadiths contain no distinction between a new grave and an exhumed one, as those who give the impurity reason claim.

Among them: he (ﷺ) cursed the Jews and Christians for taking the graves of their prophets as mosques. It is certainly known that this is not because of impurity. For that does not apply only to the graves of prophets, and the graves of prophets are among the purest places, and there is no way at all for impurity to reach them, for Allah has forbidden the earth to consume their bodies, so they are alive in their graves.

Among them: he forbade praying towards them.

Among them: he informed that the whole earth is a mosque except the graveyard and the bathhouse. Had it been because of impurity, mention of latrines and slaughterhouses and the like would have been more appropriate than mention of graves.

Among them: the site of his mosque (ﷺ) was a graveyard of the polytheists. He had their graves dug up and levelled, and took the place as a mosque, and did not remove the soil, but leveled the ground, smoothed it, and prayed in it, as established in the Two Sahihs from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

"When the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Medina and alighted at the upper part of Medina, in a quarter called Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, the Prophet (ﷺ) stayed among them for fourteen nights. Then he sent for the chiefs of Banu al-Najjar, and they came with their swords hung, and it is as if I see the Prophet (ﷺ) upon his mount, with Abu Bakr behind him, and the chiefs of Banu al-Najjar around him, until he alighted in the courtyard of Abu Ayyub.

He loved to pray wherever prayer overtook him, and he prayed in the sheepfolds. He commanded the building of the mosque, and sent for the chiefs of Banu al-Najjar and said: 'O Banu al-Najjar, name a price for this garden of yours.'

They said: 'No, by Allah, we seek its price only from Allah.' In it, as I tell you, were graves of the polytheists, and in it were ruins and palm trees. The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded that the graves of the polytheists be dug up, then the ruins were levelled, and the palm trees were cut down. They arranged the palm trees facing the qibla of the mosque, and made its two side posts of stone. They began carrying the rock, and they were chanting rajaz."

And he mentioned the hadith...

Among them: the fitna of shirk through praying at graves and imitating idol-worshippers is far greater than the harm of praying after ʿAsr and Fajr. So if this is forbidden as a blocking of the pretext of imitation, which hardly occurs to the one praying, how much more so this near pretext which often leads its doer to shirk and calling upon the dead, seeking their help, asking them for needs, and believing that prayer at their graves is better than in the mosques, and other things which are open opposition to Allah and His Messenger.

Where then is the reasoning of impurity of the place in relation to this corruption?

And among what shows that the Prophet (ﷺ) intended to protect this community from the trial with graves, as the people of Noah and those after them were tried by them:

Among them: he cursed those who take mosques upon them. Had it been because of impurity, it would have been possible to build a mosque upon them while plastering them with pure clay, and the curse would cease, and this is certainly false.

Among them: he linked in the curse those who take mosques over them with those who light lamps upon them. They are companions in the curse.

And they are equal in committing a major sin. For everything the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed is a major sin, and it is known that lighting lamps upon them was cursed only because it is a means to venerating them and making them a shrine to which the polytheists resort, as is the reality. Likewise taking mosques over them.

That is why he linked them. For taking mosques over them is veneration of them and an exposure to the trial through them. Thus Allah, glory be to Him, related of those who prevailed over the affair of the People of the Cave that they said: ﴿We will surely take over them a place of worship﴾ [al-Kahf: 21].

Among them: the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"O Allah, do not make my grave an idol that is worshipped. The anger of Allah has intensified against a people who took the graves of their prophets as mosques."

He mentioned this right after his words: "O Allah, do not make my grave an idol that is worshipped," as an indication of the cause for the curse falling upon them, namely their means to make them idols worshipped.

In sum, whoever has knowledge of shirk, its causes and its pretexts, and understood from the Messenger (ﷺ) his intentions, will be certain beyond any doubt that this emphasis of his in cursing and forbidding, with both its forms, "do not do" and "I forbid you," is not because of impurity, but because of the impurity of shirk that attaches to whoever disobeys him, commits what he forbade, follows his desire, does not fear his Lord and Master, and whose share is small or nonexistent in realizing the testimony that there is no god but Allah. For this and similar things from the Prophet (ﷺ) are a protection of the sanctuary of monotheism from being touched and covered by shirk, and a dedication to it and anger for his Lord lest anything be equated with Him.

But the polytheists refused except to disobey his command and commit what he forbade, and Satan deceived them.

He said: "Rather, this is veneration of the graves of shaykhs and the righteous."

"The more you venerate them, and the more extreme you are about them, the closer you will be to them in happiness, and the farther from their enemies."

By the life of Allah, it was through this very door that entry was made upon the worshippers of Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr, and through it entry was made upon the worshippers of idols from their time until the Day of Resurrection. The polytheists combined extremism regarding them with defaming their path, while Allah guided the people of monotheism to follow their path, and to place them in the station Allah placed them: servitude, and the stripping away from them of the distinctive attributes of divinity. This is the utmost of veneration and obedience to them.

As for the polytheists, they disobeyed their command, and belittled them in the form of veneration.

Al-Shafiʿi said: "I dislike that a created being be venerated to the extent that his grave is made a mosque, out of fear of the trial upon him and upon those after him among the people."

Among those who gave the reason as shirk and imitation of the Jews and Christians: al-Athram, in his book "Nasikh al-Hadith wa Mansukhuhu." He said, after mentioning the hadith of Abu Saʿid that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The earth has been made a mosque for me, except the graveyard and the bathhouse," and the hadith of Zayd ibn Jubayr from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from Nafi' from Ibn ʿUmar that the Prophet (ﷺ) "forbade prayer in seven places, and mentioned among them the graveyard":

Al-Athram said: "I only disliked prayer in the graveyard because of imitation of the People of the Book, for they take the graves of their prophets and righteous ones as mosques."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 71, verse 21–24 (part 1 of 2):

Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both):
"These are the names of righteous men from the people of Nuh. When they died, Satan inspired their people: 'Set up stone idols (ansab) at the gathering places where they used to sit, and name them after them.' They did so, but they were not worshipped until those (people) died and knowledge was forgotten, and then they were worshipped."

Ibn Jarir said, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: "They were righteous men among the children of Adam. They had followers who emulated them. When they died, their companions, who used to emulate them, said: 'If we made their images, it would be more stirring for us to worship when we remember them.' So they made their images. When they died and others came after them, Iblis crept up to them and said: 'They used only to worship them, and by them rain was sought, so they worshipped them.'"

Hisham ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kalbi said: My father informed me, who said:
"The first idol-worship occurred when Adam (peace be upon him) died. The sons of Shith ibn Adam placed him in a cave on the mountain upon which Adam had been sent down, in the land of India. The mountain is called Nudh, and it is the most fertile mountain on earth."

Hisham said: My father informed me, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The sons of Shith (peace be upon him) would come to the body of Adam in the cave, glorify it, and pray for mercy upon him. A man from the sons of Qabil ibn Adam said: 'O sons of Qabil, the sons of Shith have a rite they perform around it, glorifying it, and you have nothing.' So he carved an idol for them, and he was the first to make it."

Hisham said: My father also informed me: "Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr were righteous people who died in one month. Their close relatives grieved for them. A man from the sons of Qabil said: 'O people, would you like me to carve for you five idols in their likenesses? However, I cannot put spirits into them.' They said: 'Yes.' So he carved for them five idols in their likenesses and set them up for them. A man would go to his brother, his uncle, and his cousin, glorify it, and circle around it, until that first generation passed away. These had been made in the time of Barad ibn Mahla'il ibn Qaynan ibn Anush ibn Shith ibn Adam. Then another generation came and glorified them more intensely than the first generation. Then came a third generation after them, and they said: 'Our forefathers only glorified these because they hoped for their intercession with Allah, the Exalted.' So they worshipped them, magnified their matter, and their disbelief grew severe. Allah sent to them Idris (peace be upon him) as a prophet, and he called them, but they denied him. So Allah raised him to a lofty place. Their matter continued to intensify," as Ibn al-Kalbi related from Abu al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, "until Nuh (peace be upon him) came, and Allah sent him as a prophet. He was then four hundred and eighty years old. He called them to Allah in his prophethood for one hundred and twenty years, but they disobeyed and denied him. Allah commanded him to build the Ark. He finished it and boarded it when he was six hundred years old. Those who were to drown drowned, and he remained after that three hundred and fifty years, calling them to Allah."

And there were two thousand two hundred years between Adam and Nuh. The water carried these idols from land to land until it cast them onto the land of Jeddah. When the water receded and they were left on the shore, the wind blew sand over them until it covered them."

I say: The apparent meaning of the Qur'an contradicts this, and that Nuh (peace be upon him) remained among his people for a thousand years less fifty years, and that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, destroyed them by drowning after they had lived among them for this period.

Al-Kalbi said: 'Amr ibn Luhayy was a soothsayer who had a familiar spirit from the jinn: "Hasten the departure and the journey from Tihama, with fortune and safety." He said: "Jir (go), and do not stay." He said: "Go to the sandbank of Jeddah, and you will find there idols prepared. Bring them to Tihama and do not be unsettled, then call the Arabs to worship them, and they will respond." So he went to the river of Jeddah, extracted them, then carried them until he arrived at Tihama. The pilgrimage season came, and he called the Arabs to worship them, all of them. 'Awf ibn 'Adhra ibn Zayd al-Lat, son of Rufayda ibn Thawr ibn Kalb ibn Wabara ibn Taghlib ibn Hulwan ibn Imran ibn al-Haf ibn Qudha'a, responded to him, and he gave him Wadd. He carried it and it was at Wadi al-Qura, at Dumat al-Jandal. He named his son 'Abd-Wadd, and he was the first to be named with it. He appointed 'Arf, his son 'Amir, who is called 'Amir al-Ajdar, as its custodian. His descendants continued to serve it until Allah brought Islam."

Al-Kalbi said: "Malik ibn Harithah told me that he saw Wadd. He said: 'My father used to send me with milk to it, and he would say: "Give your god to drink," and I would drink it.' He said: 'Then I saw Khalid ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) after he broke it, and he made it into fragments.'"

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to demolish it, but the Banu 'Adhra and the Banu 'Amir al-Ajdar prevented him from demolishing it. He fought them, killed them, demolished it and broke it.

Al-Kalbi said: "I said to Malik ibn Harithah: 'Describe Wadd to me, as if I were looking at it.' He said: 'It was the statue of a man, as large as the greatest of men, decorated (dubbira, i.e., carved) with two garments: wrapped in one garment and covered with another. On it was a sword that he wore on his shoulder, and he had slung a bow, and before him was a spear with a banner, and a quiver containing arrows,' meaning a case."

He said: "The narration returned."

He said: "Amr ibn Luhayy also answered Mudar ibn Nizar. He gave to a man from Hudhayl called al-Harith ibn Tamim ibn Sa'd ibn Hudhayl ibn Mudrikah ibn Ilyas ibn Mudar: Suwa'. It was in a land called Wahat, in the valley of Nakhla, and those near to it from Mudar worshipped it."

Regarding this, a man of the Arabs said:
"You see them around their qibla, devoted, as Hudhayl devoted themselves to Suwa'.
Its surroundings lie slain before it, the treasures of every shepherd."

Mudhhij answered him, so he gave to An'um ibn 'Amr al-Muradi Yaghuth. It was on a hill in Yemen, worshipped by Mudhhij and those allied to them.

Hamdan answered him, so he gave to Malik ibn Murthid ibn Jushum ibn Hashid ibn Jushum ibn Khayran ibn Nawf ibn Hamdan: Ya'uq. It was in a village called Khayawan, worshipped by Hamdan and those allied to them from Yemen.

Himyar answered: he gave to a man from Dhu Ru'ayn called Ma'd Yakrib: Nasr. It was in a place in the land of Saba called Balkha', worshipped by Himyar and those allied to them. They continued to worship it until Dhu Nawas made them Jews.

These idols continued to be worshipped until Allah sent the Prophet (ﷺ), who demolished and broke them.

I say: This is an explanation of what al-Bukhari mentioned in his Sahih from Ibn 'Abbas, who said:
"The idols that were among the people of Nuh passed into the Arabs. As for Wadd, it belonged to Kalb at Dumat al-Jandal. As for Suwa', it belonged to Hudhayl. As for Yaghuth, it belonged to Murad, then to the Banu Ghutayf, at al-Huruf near Saba. As for Ya'uq, it belonged to Hamdan. As for Nasr, it belonged to Himyar, to the family of Dhu al-Kala'. He said: 'These are the names of righteous men from the people of Nuh.'"

And he mentioned what preceded.

In the Sahih of al-Bukhari, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:
"I saw 'Amr ibn 'Amir al-Khuza'i dragging his intestines in the Fire, and he was the first to release the sawa'ib (free-roaming beasts)."

In another wording: "and he altered the religion of Ibrahim."

Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith al-Taymi related to me that Abu Salih al-Samman told him that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to Aktham ibn al-Jawn al-Khuza'i:
"O Aktham, I saw 'Amr ibn Luhayy ibn Qam'ah ibn Khindif dragging his intestines in the Fire. I have never seen a man more similar to a man than he is to you, nor you to him." Aktham said: "May his likeness harm me, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "No, you are a believer and he is a disbeliever. He was the first to alter the religion of Isma'il: he set up idols, slit the ears of the she-camel (bahira), released the free-roaming beast (sa'iba), made the she-camel that bears ten young ones a wasila, and protected the stallion (ham)."

Ibn Hisham said: Some of the people of knowledge related to me: "'Amr ibn Luhayy went out from Mecca to Syria on some of his affairs. When he arrived at Ma'ab in the land of al-Balqa', where the 'Amaliqah were at that time, sons of 'Amlaq ibn Lawidh ibn Sam ibn Nuh, he saw them worshipping idols. He said to them: 'What are these idols that you worship?' They said: 'We seek rain by them, and they give us rain; we seek victory by them, and they give us victory.' He said: 'Will you not give me one of them, so that I may take it to the land of the Arabs and they may worship it?' So they gave him an idol called Hubal. He came with it to Mecca, set it up, and commanded the people to worship and glorify it."

Hisham said: My father and others related to me: "When Isma'il (peace be upon him) settled in Mecca and his children were born there, they multiplied until they filled Mecca, and they expelled those of the 'Amaliqah who were there. Mecca became too narrow for them, wars and enmities arose among them, and some of them expelled others. So they spread out across the lands seeking livelihood. What led them to worship idols and stones was that no traveler would depart from Mecca without carrying with him a stone from the stones of the Haram, out of reverence for the Haram and longing for Mecca. Wherever they settled they would place it and circle it as they circled the House, out of love for the House and longing for it. They still glorified the House and Mecca, performed the hajj and 'umrah, upon the inheritance of Ibrahim and Isma'il (peace be upon them both). Then they worshipped what they found good and forgot what they had been upon, and they exchanged the religion of Ibrahim for another, worshipping idols, and they came to be like the nations before them. They brought out from the idols what the people of Nuh had worshipped, following what remained of their memory among them. Among them there remained, from the time of Ibrahim and Isma'il, remnants of worship, by which they practised devotion: glorifying the House, circling it, the hajj and 'umrah, standing at 'Arafat and Muzdalifah, and offering the sacrificial camels, while introducing into it what was not part of it." Nizar used to say in their talbiyah:
"Here I am, O Allah, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner."
"Except a partner who is Yours, You possess him and he does not possess."

They affirmed His oneness by the talbiyah, yet they brought their gods alongside Him and made their ownership in His hand. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to His Prophet (ﷺ):
﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah without associating others with Him.﴾ [Yusuf: 106]
That is, they do not affirm My oneness with true knowledge of My right, except that they set up a partner alongside Me from among My creation.

The talbiyah of 'Akk, when they set out as pilgrims, was that they sent two black boys ahead of them. They would walk in front of their caravan and say:
"We are the two crows of 'Akk."
Then 'Akk would say after them:
"'Akk, to You is your servant, the Yemenite servants of Yours."

When Rabi'ah performed the hajj and completed the rites and stood at the standing-places, they would depart in the first group and not remain until the last days of Tashriq.

The first to alter the religion of Isma'il, setting up idols, releasing the free-roaming beast (sa'iba), slitting the ears of the she-camel (bahira), making the wasila, and protecting the stallion (ham), was 'Amr ibn Rabi'ah, who is Luhayy ibn Harithah ibn 'Amr ibn 'Amir al-Azdi, and he is the father of Khuza'ah.

The mother of 'Amr was Fuhayrah bint 'Amir ibn al-Harith; it is also said Qam'ah bint Mudad. The Harith who was in charge of the affairs of the Ka'bah, when 'Amr ibn Luhayy came of age, disputed the leadership with him, and he fought Jurhum with the sons of Isma'il. He defeated them, drove them out from the Ka'bah, and expelled them from the lands of Mecca.

He took over the guardianship of the House after them. Then he fell severely ill, and it was said to him: "In al-Balqa' of Syria there is hot springs; if you go there you will be healed." He went there, bathed in it, and was healed. He found its people worshipping idols and said: "What are these?" They said: "We seek rain by them and seek victory over the enemy by them." He asked them to give him some of them, and they did, so he brought them to Mecca and set them up around the Ka'bah.

The Arabs adopted idols. The earliest of them was Manat, and the Arabs used to name themselves 'Abd Manat and Zayd Manat. It was set up on the seacoast in the direction of al-Mushallal near Qudayd, between Mecca and Medina, and all the Arabs glorified it. The Aws and Khazraj and those who lived in Medina and Mecca and the nearby places glorified it, slaughtering for it and offering gifts to it. The sons of Ma'd were upon a remnant of the religion of Isma'il. Rabi'ah and Mudar were upon a remnant of his religion, and none were more intense in glorifying it than the Aws and Khazraj.

Hisham said: A man of Quraysh related to us from Abu 'Ubaydah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi 'Ubaydah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ammar ibn Yasir, who said:
"The Aws and Khazraj and those who neighboured them from the Arabs of Yathrib and elsewhere used to perform the hajj, standing with the people at all the standing-places. They did not shave their heads. When they dispersed, they would come to it and shave their heads there, and they remained there, not regarding their hajj as complete except by that."

Manat belonged to Hudhayl and Khuza'ah. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) sent 'Ali, who demolished it in the year of the Conquest.

Then they took al-Lat at al-Ta'if, which was more recent than Manat. It was a square rock, and a Jew used to grind sawiq (parched grain) at it. Its custodians were the Banu 'Attab ibn Malik of Thaqif, and they had built a structure over it. Quraysh and all the Arabs glorified it, and by it the Arabs used to name themselves Zayd al-Lat and Taym al-Lat. It was at the place where the left minaret of the mosque of al-Ta'if stands today.

It remained so until Thaqif embraced Islam. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who demolished it and burned it with fire.

Then they took al-Uzza, which was more recent than al-Lat and Manat. Zalim ibn As'ad took it. It was in a valley of Nakhlah al-Shamiyah called Hurad, opposite al-Ghumayr, on the right side of the one ascending to Iraq from Mecca. That is beyond Dhat 'Irq, and they built a house over it. They used to hear a sound from it.

Hisham said: My father related to me from Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-'Uzza was a female devil who came to three acacia trees in the valley of Nakhlah. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Mecca, he sent Khalid ibn al-Walid, saying: 'Go to the valley of Nakhlah, for you will find three acacias; cut down the first.' He went and cut it down. When he came back to him, he said: 'Did you see anything?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Cut down the second.' He went and cut it down. Then he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'Did you see anything?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Cut down the third.' He went and found an Abyssinian woman with disheveled hair, placing her hands on her shoulders, gnashing with her fangs, and behind her was Dubayyah ibn Hurmi al-Shaybani, then al-Sulami, who was her custodian. When she saw Khalid, she said:
'O 'Uzza, strike with strength, do not be false, against Khalid, cast off your veil and gird up your skirts.
For if you do not kill Khalid today, you will be humiliated quickly and be made Christian.'
Khalid said:
'O 'Uzza, disbelief in you, no glorification of you, for I have seen that Allah has humiliated you.'
Then he struck her and split her head, and she was a black lump of charcoal. Then he cut down the tree, and killed the custodian, and then came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him. He said: 'That was al-'Uzza, and there will be no 'Uzza for the Arabs after her. Indeed, she will not be worshipped after today.'"

(Section)

Among the greatest of his schemes, by which he deceived most people, and from which none escaped except those whom Allah did not intend to test, is what he inspired, from of old and in recent times, into his party and allies: the temptation through graves. Until the matter ended with them worshipping their masters besides Allah, and their graves were worshipped, and they took them as idols, built temples over them, carved the images of their masters in them, then those images became bodies with shadows, then they were made idols and worshipped alongside Allah, the Exalted.

The beginning of this great disease was among the people of Nuh, as He, glorified is He, told of them in His Book, where He says:
﴿Nuh said: "My Lord, they disobeyed me and followed one whom his wealth and children increased only in loss. And they schemed a great scheme. And they said: 'Do not leave your gods; do not leave Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr.' And they have led many astray..."﴾ [Nuh: 21–24]

Ibn Jarir said:
"What was reported to us about these was what Ibn Humayd related to us: Mahran related to us from Sufyan from Musa from Muhammad ibn Qays, that Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr were righteous men among the children of Adam. They had followers who emulated them. When they died, their companions who used to emulate them said: 'If we made their images, it would be more stirring for us to worship when we remember them.' So they made their images. When they died and others came after them, Iblis crept up to them and said: 'They only worshipped them, and by them rain was sought, so they worshipped them.'"

Sufyan related from his father from 'Ikrimah, who said: "Between Adam and Nuh (peace be upon them both) there were ten generations, all upon Islam."

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us from Ma'mar from Qatadah regarding this verse, who said: "They were gods worshipped by the people of Nuh, and then the Arabs worshipped them after that. Wadd was for Kalb at Dumat al-Jandal, and Suwa' was for Hudhayl. Yaghuth was for the Banu Ghutayf of Murad. Ya'uq was for Hamdan. Nasr was for Dhu al-Kala' of Himyar."

Al-Walibi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "These are idols that were worshipped in the time of Nuh (peace be upon him)."

Al-Bukhari said: Ibrahim ibn Musa related to us: Hisham related to us from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' said from Ibn 'Abbas:
"The idols that were among the people of Nuh passed into the Arabs after that.
As for Wadd, it belonged to Kalb at Dumat al-Jandal.
As for Suwa', it belonged to Hudhayl."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 71, verse 21–24 (part 2 of 2):

As for Yaghuth, it belonged to Murad, then to the Banu Ghutayf at al-Jurf near Saba'.
As for Ya'uq, it belonged to Hamdan.
As for Nasr, it belonged to Himyar, to the family of Dhu al-Kala'.

They were the names of righteous men from the people of Noah. When they died, Satan inspired their people to set up idols (anṣāb) at the gatherplaces where they used to sit, and to name them after them. They did so, but they were not worshipped until those men had died and knowledge had been forgotten, and then they were worshipped."

Another scholar among the early generations (al-salaf) said: These were righteous men among the people of Noah, peace be upon him. When they died, the people remained devoted at their graves, then they made images of them, then time lengthened over them and they worshipped them.

These people combined two trials: the trial of graves and the trial of images. These are the two trials to which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pointed in the hadith agreed upon as authentic, narrated from ʿĀʾisha (may Allah be pleased with her):

"Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her) mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a church she had seen in the land of Abyssinia, called Maria. She described to him the images she had seen in it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Those are a people who, when a righteous servant or a righteous man among them died, built a place of worship (masjid) over his grave and made those images in it. Those are the worst of creation in the sight of Allah, the Exalted.'"

In another wording in the Two Sahihs:

"Umm Habibah and Umm Salamah mentioned a church they had seen."

So in this hadith he combined images and graves, and this was the cause of the worship of al-Lat.

Ibn Jarir narrated with his chain from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding:

﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-ʿUzza?﴾ [al-Najm: 19]

He said: "He used to knead the sawiq (a porridge of roasted grain) for them. When he died, they remained devoted at his grave." Similarly Abu al-Jawza said, from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both):

"He used to knead the sawiq for the pilgrims."

Thus you have seen that the cause of the worship of Wadd, Yaghuth, Ya'uq, Nasr and al-Lat was only the veneration of their graves, and then they made images of them and worshipped them, as the Prophet (ﷺ) indicated.

My shaykh said: "This is the reason for which the Lawgiver forbade taking mosques upon graves, and it is what led many nations either into major shirk or into what is less than it. Souls have associated partners with Allah through the images of righteous people, and through images they claim are talismans for the stars and the like. Shirk directed at the grave of a man believed to be righteous is closer to souls than shirk directed at a piece of wood or a stone. This is why we find the people of shirk often humbling themselves there, becoming submissive and lowly, and worshipping them in their hearts with a worship they do not perform in the houses of Allah or at the time of dawn. Some of them prostrate to them. Most of them hope for blessing from prayer and supplication there what they do not hope for in the mosques.

Because of this corruption, the Prophet (ﷺ) cut off its source, to the extent that he forbade prayer in the graveyard absolutely, even if the one praying does not intend the blessing of the place by his prayer, as he intends the blessing of the mosques. Likewise he forbade prayer at the time of sunrise and sunset, because these are times when the polytheists intend to pray to the sun. So he forbade his community to pray at those times, even if the one praying does not intend what the polytheists intended, as a blocking of the means (sadd al-dhara'i')."

He said: As for when a man intends to pray at graves seeking blessing by praying in that spot, this is precisely deceiving Allah and His Messenger, opposing His religion, and innovating a religion Allah did not permit. The Muslims have agreed, on what they know necessarily from the religion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that praying at graves is forbidden, and that he cursed whoever takes them as mosques. So among the greatest innovations and causes of shirk is praying at them and taking them as mosques, and building mosques upon them. The texts from the Prophet, peace be upon him, forbidding this and warning strongly against it have been transmitted by multiple chains. Most schools have explicitly stated the prohibition of building mosques over them, following the sound and clear Sunnah. The companions of Ahmad and others from the companions of Malik and al-Shafiʿi have explicitly stated its prohibition. A group stated it as merely disliked (makruh) without qualification. What should be understood is that it refers to the disliked in the sense of prohibition (karahat al-tahrim), out of good opinion of the scholars, and one should not think of them that they would permit what has been transmitted by multiple chains from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as cursing its doer and forbidding it. In Sahih Muslim, from Jundub ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Bajali, who said:

I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) five days before he died saying:

"I disown before Allah that I should have a close friend (khalil) among you. Indeed Allah has taken me as a close friend, as He took Ibrahim as a close friend. Had I taken a close friend from my community, I would have taken Abu Bakr as a close friend. Beware, those before you used to take the graves of their prophets as mosques. Beware, do not take graves as mosques, for I forbid you from that."

And from ʿĀʾisha and ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas, who both said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was near death, he began placing a cloak over his face, and when he felt distress he uncovered it, and he said, while in that state: 'The curse of Allah be upon the Jews and the Christians, who took the graves of their prophets as mosques,' warning against what they did."

Agreed upon.

Also in the Two Sahihs, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him):

That the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah fight the Jews and the Christians, who took the graves of their prophets as mosques."

In Muslim's narration: "May Allah curse the Jews and the Christians, who took the graves of their prophets as mosques."

So he forbade taking graves as mosques at the end of his life, and then he cursed, while in his last moments, those from the People of the Book who did that, in order to warn his community against doing the same.

ʿĀʾisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said during his illness from which he did not rise: "May Allah curse the Jews and the Christians, who took the graves of their prophets as mosques. Had it not been for that, his grave would have been made conspicuous, but it was feared that it would be taken as a mosque."

Agreed upon.

Her words "khushiya" (it was feared) are with a damma on the kha', as the reason for not exposing his grave.

Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad, with a good chain, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Among the most evil of people are those on whom the Hour will come while they are alive, and those who take graves as mosques."

From Zayd ibn Thabit, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah curse the Jews, who took the graves of their prophets as mosques." Narrated by Imam Ahmad.

From Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the women who visit graves, and those who take mosques and lamps upon them." Narrated by Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan.

In Sahih al-Bukhari: that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) saw Anas ibn Malik praying at a grave, and said: "The grave! The grave!" This shows that it was well established among the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) that their Prophet had forbidden them to pray at graves. Anas's action (may Allah be pleased with him) does not indicate his belief in its permissibility, for perhaps he had not seen it, or did not know it was a grave, or he was heedless of it. When ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) alerted him, he became mindful.

Abu Saʿid al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The whole earth is a mosque except the graveyard and the bathhouse."

Narrated by Imam Ahmad and the authors of the four Sunan, and authenticated by Abu Hatim Ibn Hibban.

More emphatic than this: he forbade praying facing a grave, so that a grave is not between the one praying and the qibla.

Muslim narrated in his Sahih, from Abu Marthad al-Ghanawi (may Allah have mercy on him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not sit upon graves, and do not pray facing them."

In this is a refutation of the view of those who claim that the prohibition of praying there is due to impurity (najasa). This is the furthest thing from the intentions of the Messenger (ﷺ), and it is false for several reasons:

Among them: the hadiths contain no distinction between a new grave and an exhumed one, as those who give the impurity reason claim.

Among them: he (ﷺ) cursed the Jews and Christians for taking the graves of their prophets as mosques. It is certainly known that this is not because of impurity. For that does not apply only to the graves of prophets, and the graves of prophets are among the purest places, and there is no way at all for impurity to reach them, for Allah has forbidden the earth to consume their bodies, so they are alive in their graves.

Among them: he forbade praying towards them.

Among them: he informed that the whole earth is a mosque except the graveyard and the bathhouse. Had it been because of impurity, mention of latrines and slaughterhouses and the like would have been more appropriate than mention of graves.

Among them: the site of his mosque (ﷺ) was a graveyard of the polytheists. He had their graves dug up and levelled, and took the place as a mosque, and did not remove the soil, but leveled the ground, smoothed it, and prayed in it, as established in the Two Sahihs from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

"When the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Medina and alighted at the upper part of Medina, in a quarter called Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, the Prophet (ﷺ) stayed among them for fourteen nights. Then he sent for the chiefs of Banu al-Najjar, and they came with their swords hung, and it is as if I see the Prophet (ﷺ) upon his mount, with Abu Bakr behind him, and the chiefs of Banu al-Najjar around him, until he alighted in the courtyard of Abu Ayyub.

He loved to pray wherever prayer overtook him, and he prayed in the sheepfolds. He commanded the building of the mosque, and sent for the chiefs of Banu al-Najjar and said: 'O Banu al-Najjar, name a price for this garden of yours.'

They said: 'No, by Allah, we seek its price only from Allah.' In it, as I tell you, were graves of the polytheists, and in it were ruins and palm trees. The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded that the graves of the polytheists be dug up, then the ruins were levelled, and the palm trees were cut down. They arranged the palm trees facing the qibla of the mosque, and made its two side posts of stone. They began carrying the rock, and they were chanting rajaz."

And he mentioned the hadith...

Among them: the fitna of shirk through praying at graves and imitating idol-worshippers is far greater than the harm of praying after ʿAsr and Fajr. So if this is forbidden as a blocking of the pretext of imitation, which hardly occurs to the one praying, how much more so this near pretext which often leads its doer to shirk and calling upon the dead, seeking their help, asking them for needs, and believing that prayer at their graves is better than in the mosques, and other things which are open opposition to Allah and His Messenger.

Where then is the reasoning of impurity of the place in relation to this corruption?

And among what shows that the Prophet (ﷺ) intended to protect this community from the trial with graves, as the people of Noah and those after them were tried by them:

Among them: he cursed those who take mosques upon them. Had it been because of impurity, it would have been possible to build a mosque upon them while plastering them with pure clay, and the curse would cease, and this is certainly false.

Among them: he linked in the curse those who take mosques over them with those who light lamps upon them. They are companions in the curse.

And they are equal in committing a major sin. For everything the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed is a major sin, and it is known that lighting lamps upon them was cursed only because it is a means to venerating them and making them a shrine to which the polytheists resort, as is the reality. Likewise taking mosques over them.

That is why he linked them. For taking mosques over them is veneration of them and an exposure to the trial through them. Thus Allah, glory be to Him, related of those who prevailed over the affair of the People of the Cave that they said: ﴿We will surely take over them a place of worship﴾ [al-Kahf: 21].

Among them: the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"O Allah, do not make my grave an idol that is worshipped. The anger of Allah has intensified against a people who took the graves of their prophets as mosques."

He mentioned this right after his words: "O Allah, do not make my grave an idol that is worshipped," as an indication of the cause for the curse falling upon them, namely their means to make them idols worshipped.

In sum, whoever has knowledge of shirk, its causes and its pretexts, and understood from the Messenger (ﷺ) his intentions, will be certain beyond any doubt that this emphasis of his in cursing and forbidding, with both its forms, "do not do" and "I forbid you," is not because of impurity, but because of the impurity of shirk that attaches to whoever disobeys him, commits what he forbade, follows his desire, does not fear his Lord and Master, and whose share is small or nonexistent in realizing the testimony that there is no god but Allah. For this and similar things from the Prophet (ﷺ) are a protection of the sanctuary of monotheism from being touched and covered by shirk, and a dedication to it and anger for his Lord lest anything be equated with Him.

But the polytheists refused except to disobey his command and commit what he forbade, and Satan deceived them.

He said: "Rather, this is veneration of the graves of shaykhs and the righteous."

"The more you venerate them, and the more extreme you are about them, the closer you will be to them in happiness, and the farther from their enemies."

By the life of Allah, it was through this very door that entry was made upon the worshippers of Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr, and through it entry was made upon the worshippers of idols from their time until the Day of Resurrection. The polytheists combined extremism regarding them with defaming their path, while Allah guided the people of monotheism to follow their path, and to place them in the station Allah placed them: servitude, and the stripping away from them of the distinctive attributes of divinity. This is the utmost of veneration and obedience to them.

As for the polytheists, they disobeyed their command, and belittled them in the form of veneration.

Al-Shafiʿi said: "I dislike that a created being be venerated to the extent that his grave is made a mosque, out of fear of the trial upon him and upon those after him among the people."

Among those who gave the reason as shirk and imitation of the Jews and Christians: al-Athram, in his book "Nasikh al-Hadith wa Mansukhuhu." He said, after mentioning the hadith of Abu Saʿid that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The earth has been made a mosque for me, except the graveyard and the bathhouse," and the hadith of Zayd ibn Jubayr from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from Nafi' from Ibn ʿUmar that the Prophet (ﷺ) "forbade prayer in seven places, and mentioned among them the graveyard":

Al-Athram said: "I only disliked prayer in the graveyard because of imitation of the People of the Book, for they take the graves of their prophets and righteous ones as mosques."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 71, verse 27:

His saying: ﴿And they will not beget any but wicked disbelievers﴾

This does not contradict their being born upon the sound natural disposition (fitrah), for His saying ﴿wicked disbelievers﴾ are two circumstantial qualifiers (hal) that are anticipated (muqaddarah), meaning: whoever will commit wickedness (fujur) and disbelieve.

He also said in (Ahkam Ahl al-Dhimmah):

And they also argued with His saying, may He be exalted, reporting about Noah that he said: ﴿And they will not beget any but wicked disbelievers﴾

The wicked and the disbelievers are among the people of the Fire, and this is no proof, because he meant by it only the disbelievers of his own time, definitely. Otherwise, some of the disbelievers after them have begotten prophets, just as Azar begot Abraham the Friend (Khalil).

Also, His saying ﴿wicked disbelievers﴾ is an anticipated circumstantial qualifier (hal muqaddarah), meaning: whoever, if he lives, will be a wicked disbeliever. He did not intend by it that their infants, at the moment of their birth, would be wicked and disbelieving, as its explanation has already preceded.
